podcast.body: Alongside "Billie Jean," this track was among the initial songs to be officially licensed for use in a video game. It was featured in the Sega Genesis game *Moonwalker* in 1990, demonstrating an early collaboration between the music and video game industries. "The first proper song to be licensed for inclusion into a video game was, Michael Jackson's Billie Jean and Beat It. It was in the Sega Genesis game Moonwalker in 1990."

podcast.body: For *Beat It*, Michael Jackson deliberately expanded his musical style, incorporating rock elements and synthesizer music, genres he hadn't extensively worked with before. After auditioning numerous guitarists for the electric guitar part, he called Eddie Van Halen. Jackson made Van Halen try 30 different guitars to achieve the exact sound he envisioned for the song's chords, a process Van Halen described as an unparalleled "fetishism of sound." "Michael Jackson acabó llamando al mismo de Divaan Hallen al cual lo hizo probar 30 guitarras distintas hasta que encontró a Eddie Van Hallen y encontró la guitarra que Michael Jackson quería para cómo sonaba en el beat."

podcast.body: The video for "Beat It" was crucial in breaking MTV's unofficial color barrier. After CBS Records allegedly threatened to withdraw all their videos from the channel, MTV caved and began showing clips from the "Thriller" album, including "Beat It." Its appearance led to "Thriller" selling 200,000 copies a week. "Once the clip for Beaded appeared, thriller started selling 200,000 copies a week."
